page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64 and includes a 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 67260.4 and a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 86642.75. The memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput, reaching a read-only large block bandwidth of 326.02 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 127.56 GB/sec. The hardware excels in data processing tasks, achieving 111.2 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a top-tier static web serving throughput of 104.9 GB/sec. Additionally, the integrated AMX instructions contribute to a top-tier LLM inference prompt processing speed of 3946.15 tokens per second for small models.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a balanced allocation of compute and memory, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring both high CPU performance and fast local storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized tiers. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training. The server is highly suited for enterprise database operations, high-throughput web serving, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale LLM inference workloads.
